task: Phase 2: device roles, memberships and persistence. Domain DeviceRole/DeviceMembership, store contracts with compare-and-set (InMemory + EF), 4 EF tables per design contract §8, migration AddDeviceRolesAndMemberships (UPDATE policy_versions then DELETE device-action grants), grantor fields on feature/resource grants with migration AddPermissionGrantGrantor, DI for both branches. Additive: no handler or controller changes.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build 0 errors; dotnet test green

has-pending-model-changes reports none; AddDeviceRolesAndMemberships creates only the 4 tables with §8 indexes/FKs plus UPDATE policy_versions before DELETE device-action; AddPermissionGrantGrantor adds only 2 columns
feature/resource grants persist and read back GrantedBy/GrantedByMasterAdmin; legacy rows read null/false; positional call sites still compile
unique (UserId, DeviceId), unique (OrganizationId, NormalizedName), FK Restrict/Cascade per §8, device_roles.Version and device_memberships.RoleId are model-only concurrency tokens
Operator then operator in one organization -> DEVICE_ROLE_NAME_TAKEN from the store, nothing written; same name in another organization is fine (EF and InMemory)

membership upsert null->A->B with matching expectedRoleId -> one row, new role, 2 audits; mismatch -> DEVICE_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED without audit; remove absent with null expected -> false without audit; remove writes audit; regrant restores (EF and InMemory)
200 parallel upserts with the same expectedRoleId on InMemory -> exactly one winner, one row per (user, device)

role update stale -> DEVICE_ROLE_VERSION_STALE; remove order NOT_FOUND -> VERSION_STALE -> IN_USE without audit; successful remove deletes role, permissions and writes 1 ROLE_DELETED audit in one SaveChanges

EF lost race (concurrency token) -> DEVICE_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED / DEVICE_ROLE_VERSION_STALE; the audit row is in the same SaveChanges as the rejected write (rollback relies on the PostgreSQL transaction; EF InMemory cannot show it)
development resolves one InMemoryDeviceAccessStore for both interfaces; a connection string registers scoped EF stores
no existing test changed except Model_has_management_tables_only
publicContracts: DB schema: 4 new tables and 2 new permission_grants columns (additive); the migration deletes permission_grants rows with Kind device-action (owner decision V3, back up first)
FeaturePermissionGrant/ResourceScopeGrant gain two trailing optional parameters (source compatible)

PermissionGrantsController returns grant records as-is, so POST /permissions/features, POST /permissions/resource-scopes and GET /permissions/{userId} now also emit grantedBy (null) and grantedByMasterAdmin (false); additive, the frontend ignores them; these existing endpoints keep the grant-record shape (owner decision 2026-10-05), so every id there, grantedBy included, serializes as {value}; the contract §6 plain-Guid rule applies to new DTOs; the frontend accepts both shapes

new public types: DeviceRole, DeviceRoleId, DeviceMembership, IDeviceRoleStore, IDeviceMembershipStore, DeviceAccessAuditEntry, DeviceAccessChanges, InMemoryDeviceAccessStore, EfDeviceRoleStore, EfDeviceMembershipStore
blastRadius: EfPermissionStore feature/resource read/write paths (grant handlers, ScopeAuthorization, MeController read these records)
applying the migration to a database with data deletes legacy device-action grants that code still reads until phases 3-4 (release the whole plan at once)
scoutSummary: Store patterns: InMemory stores use _gate + lock (LicenseContracts), EF stores read AsNoTracking and report InvalidOperationException(code), reload after a failed SaveChanges with ChangeTracker.Clear (EfCommandAuditStore). DI branches on the connection string. No PostgreSQL in this environment and no git repository. The design contract (plans/261005-0556-device-permissions-what-where/reports/design-contract.md §3, §4, §8) is binding.
